sentences.text: Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms named for its broad, duck-like snout.
The broad, flattened shape of the Anatosuchus skull developed as the animal matured.
The premaxillae of Anatosuchus are broad and flat, each holding six recurved teeth that point backward.
The maxillae are the largest bones in the Anatosuchus skull, each containing nineteen small recurved teeth.
The lower jaw of Anatosuchus bears twenty-one teeth on each side.
Anatosuchus teeth were small, subconical, and showed little wear, suggesting they were not heavily used for grinding.
The largest teeth in the Anatosuchus skull are located at the corners.
The proatlas vertebra is an inverted V-shaped bone with a dorsal keel that is quite large relative to the atlas.
The neural spines on the cervical vertebrae grow taller along the series, with the third being twice as tall as long and the seventh almost five times as tall as long.
The osteoderms on Anatosuchus are trapezoidal in shape and quite pitted.
The manus features very large fourth digits with six phalanges instead of the usual four.
The humeri are long, straight, and quite slender, with a width of less than 10% of their length.
The ulnae are relatively curved.
The radiales are strong, heavy bones that are almost as wide as the radii.
A 11 mm toothless section of the lower jaw likely formed a cutting edge used with the front upper teeth to process prey.
It is currently unknown what evolutionary benefit the specialized six-phalanged fourth digits provided.
Anatosuchus was described by a team of paleontologists led by American Paul Sereno in 2003.
The fossils of Anatosuchus were discovered in Gadoufaoua, Niger.
Anatosuchus was described based on a juvenile specimen.
The holotype material (MNN GDF603) consists of an almost complete skull with articulated jaws.
Despite its duck-like appearance, Anatosuchus is considered to have eaten small aquatic creatures.
Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodile.
The genus Anatosuchus was named by Sereno et al. in 2003.
The only known species is Anatosuchus minor, described by Sereno et al. in 2003.
Anatosuchus is classified within the family Uruguaysuchidae.
Anatosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Fossils of Anatosuchus were found in the Elrhaz and Echkar Formations, dating to the Late Aptian or Early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
Anatosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the late Aptian or early Albian stages.
Anatosuchus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
Initial descriptions suggested Anatosuchus formed a monophyletic clade with Comahuesuchus within Notosuchia, though this is disputed.
